$doc: Fact's appearance, as data — the source of the `@component fact` block in css/components.css and of dist/react/fact.tsx. Same contract as components/button/definition.json: a plain string is a structural literal, {"token": "x"} binds --x, and an array is a sequence of both. FACT IS THE FIRST BLOCK WITH AN `at` BLOCK, and it is the smallest possible case for one: below 720px the row of facts stacks, so the divider that was on the right edge has to be on the bottom. The condition is a NAME resolved in tokens.json's `$conditions` rather than the string `(max-width: 720px)`, because `entry` writes the same number for the same reason and nothing said so. It is also where `last` joined the position vocabulary: the divider is drawn by every fact and undrawn by the final one, in both the row and the stack, which is two rules that only a sibling position can write.

rules.$doc: The frame. `gap: 0` is deliberate and is the reason the dividers work: the facts touch, so one border between two of them is one line rather than two with a gutter.

rules.name: fact
rules.$doc: One figure. `flex: 1 1 14rem` is the whole responsive behaviour above the breakpoint — facts share the row until one would be narrower than 14rem, and then they wrap.

rules.name: closing
rules.$doc: The last fact drops its divider, so the run of them ends on the frame rather than on a line inside it. A position rather than a modifier, because no fact knows how many siblings it has and the markup should not have to say.

rules.name: num
rules.$doc: The figure itself, at the display step and the widest step of the display family's width axis. `tabular-nums` so a column of figures lines up on the digit rather than on the glyph.

rules.name: unit
rules.$doc: The suffix riding on the number — the % or the ×. It binds --text-unit, which is an em RATIO rather than a step: it means "a fraction of whatever set me", so it follows the display number through every clamp the number goes through.

rules.name: title
rules.$doc: The mono chrome label above the figure — the same family, case and tracking step as a chip, a plate label and the sources heading.

rules.name: label
rules.$doc: The sentence under the figure. Body prose at the small step, so a fact reads as a claim with a number rather than as a number with a caption.

Stacked, the divider turns ninety degrees. It is the same two rules as above — every fact draws one, the last one does not — with the edge changed, which is what makes this an override of a named rule rather than a second definition of it.

The same last-child rule as above, restated for the stacked edge. It NAMES the position rather than nesting one: `closing` is a rule with a handle, so an override can point at it exactly as it points at `fact`, and `override.positions` — the last place in this format where a rule lived inside another rule — retired with it.
